# Prompt Injection Defenses in Agent Orchestrators

## TL;DR

Multi-agent orchestrators create attack surfaces absent in single-agent systems:
inter-agent injection, tool-call manipulation, memory poisoning, and confused
deputy chains. Architectural defenses (SEAgent MAC, Progent DSL, CaMeL
capability tokens) achieve 0% attack success rate on benchmarks, but none are
deployed in production. Detection-based defenses fail on orchestrator-specific
attack surfaces — classifiers designed for user input miss inter-agent and
tool-output injection. The practical defense strategy is defense-in-depth:
deterministic tool controls, architectural separation, output sanitization,
sandboxing, and short-lived credentials — designed for containment, not
prevention.

| Prompt Shields (Microsoft) [25] | Unknown | Low | API classifier | Production |
| SK Filters [26] | N/A (deterministic) | None | Code-level hooks | Production |

## Key Attack Vectors (Orchestrator-Specific)

| Attack | ASR | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Control-flow hijacking [1] | 58-100% | Untrusted content hijacks orchestrator |
| Tool poisoning (MCP) [28] | — | Hidden instructions in tool descriptions |
| Memory injection (MINJA) [9] | 70% | Query-only memory corruption |
| RAG poisoning (AgentPoison) [10] | ≥80% | <0.1% poison rate backdoor |
| Contagious jailbreak (ARCJ) [11] | +23-53% | Self-replicating viral propagation |
| Approval bypass [29][41] | — | Argument injection, lies-in-the-loop |

## Quick Decision Framework

1. **Assume breach.** Design for containment, not prevention. "Prompt injection
   attacks are inevitable" (Microsoft [25]).

2. **Separate architecturally.** Never pass untrusted data directly to
   privileged agents. Dual-LLM [15] or agent isolation [5] at minimum.

3. **Enforce tool access deterministically.** Use code-level policy (ABAC,
   DSL, filters [4][7][26]), not prompt-based guardrails.

4. **Sanitize tool outputs.** Output firewalls between tool results and
   downstream agents achieve near-complete mitigation [17].

5. **Sandbox execution.** MicroVM or gVisor for any agent executing code or
   shell commands.

6. **Short-lived credentials.** Scoped to the specific task, revoked on
   completion.

7. **Layer detection and monitoring.** PromptArmor (<1% FPR [16]) + canary
   tokens + behavioral baselines.
